To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel Parameter Remapping technique for Fast Neural Network Adaptations that can adapt the architecture and parameters in a network to obtain networks with new depth, width, and kernel sizes, and we show that the adapted networks out-perform both manually designed networks and networks obtained by NAS.

we propose FNA, which adapts a seed network to become a new network with different depth and width, and we show FNA out-performs SOTA networks designed both manually (MobileNetV2) and by NAS (Auto-DeepLab and DetNAS), while being significantly more efficient than SOTA NAS approaches.

we propose a fast neural network adaptation method which adapts both the architecture and the parameters of a seed neural network, and can obtain new networks with better performance than SOTA networks designed both manually or by NAS, while being computationally efficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three questions.

improving the efficiency of NAS for semantic segmentation and object detectors, by proposing a novel FNA approach that can adapt the architecture and parameters to become a network of different depth, width or kernel size, with a significantly reduced computational cost.

the following three questions:
    - Can we adapt a network to a new architecture with different depth, kernels or width, and still retain its original performance?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FNA is a novel method that can significantly reduce computational cost for both segmentation and object detection tasks, while achieving SOTA performance.
we propose a fast and efficient method for adapting the architecture and parameters to achieve SOTA performance on segmentation and detection tasks.
we propose a new method, FNA, to efficiently adapt a seed network into a new network with different depth or width.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel method for adapting a network to have a different depth/width/kernels, making it possible and practical to apply NAS for segmentation/detection tasks.
we can obtain new architectures for both segmentation and object detection, which outperform the SOTA manually designed or NAS approaches, while using only a small fraction of the computational cost.
we can obtain new SOTA networks for detection and segmentation with a fraction of the cost of the SOTA NAS approaches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can obtain SOTA networks for detection/segmentaion by using FNA to adapt a manually designed backbone.

we show that NAS for detection and segmentation can be conducted much more efficiently by using a parameter remapping approach, and we demonstrate that this is an effective way of obtaining new SOTA networks for detection and segmentation.
FNA is a simple and efficient approach that can be used to improve the performance of existing networks for detection and segmentation tasks.
